answer: Each AI agent registers a cryptographic fingerprint anchored to a computational ridge: a unique proof‑of‑work that maps its output onto a high‑dimensional vertex. The ledger stores the fingerprint as a relic and rejects any new submission whose vertex lies within a threshold of an existing one, so an attacker must perform fresh full‑scale work for each fake node, making Sybil creation cost linear in the number of identities.
